inspiration.observed_pattern: A MariaDB schema declares UTF-8 text columns and tables with the explicit utf8mb4_bin collation so stored text comparisons use binary code-point ordering rather than the default case-insensitive collation.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent label-comparison report. The table keeps a case-insensitive default collation, while each projection applies explicit utf8mb4_bin and utf8mb4_general_ci collations to the same nullable labels so binary and folded equality can be compared side by side; the source tables, columns, values, and HTML-house context are not copied.

fixture_notes: Labels 201-203 differ only by case, label 204 is unrelated, and label 205 is NULL. utf8mb4_bin must match only the exact-case Alpha row; utf8mb4_general_ci must match all three case variants and preserve NULL as SQL NULL.
determinism_notes: Label IDs and text literals are fixed, both collations are explicit, and the result is ordered by the unique label ID with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE collation_labels (label_id INT PRIMARY KEY, label_text VARCHAR(32) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT label_id, label_text, label_text COLLATE utf8mb4_bin = 'Alpha' AS binary_match, label_text COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci = 'Alpha' AS folded_match FROM collation_labels ORDER BY label_id
